# Bialgebras with vanishing Verschiebung are generated by primitive elements

Author: Worker 1519, as internal infrastructure for the proof of
`Langlands.GroupScheme.RelativeRoot.SmoothCommutativePTorsionVectorStatement`.

Provenance: internal. The result is the classical fact that a coconnected commutative
cocommutative Hopf algebra in characteristic `p` whose dual has vanishing `p`-th powers on the
augmentation ideal is generated by its primitive elements; the Lean argument below (an
induction along the coradical filtration with an explicit multilinear reconstruction) is the
author's own implementation, and no source statement is translated.

Notation: `k` is a field, `A` a commutative and cocommutative `k`-bialgebra, the convolution
dual is `WithConv (A →ₗ[k] k)` and `augIdeal` its ideal of functionals vanishing at `1`.

## Generic ideal facts

- `prod_mem_pow_card`: a product over a finite set `s` of elements of an ideal `I` lies in
  `I ^ s.card`.
- `mem_pow_closure I n`: every element of `I ^ n` lies in the additive closure of the
  elements `d * ∏ t : Fin n, η t` with all `η t ∈ I`.

## Elements killed by powers of the augmentation ideal

- `killedBy J`: the subspace of `A` of elements killed by every functional in the ideal `J`;
  `killedBy (augIdeal ^ (m + 1))` is the `m`-th step of the coradical filtration.
- `smul_apply'`, `sub_apply'`, `one_apply'`, `sum_apply'`: evaluation of scalar multiples,
  differences, the unit (the counit) and finite sums of functionals.
- `sub_smul_one_mem_augIdeal θ`: `θ - θ 1 • 1 ∈ augIdeal`.
- `eq_counit_smul_one_of_mem_killedBy`: an element killed by `augIdeal` equals
  `counit a • 1`.
- `isPrimitiveElem_of_mem_killedBy`: an element with `counit x = 0` killed by `augIdeal ^ 2`
  is primitive. The two sides of `comul x = 1 ⊗ x + x ⊗ 1` are compared after contracting
  with all pairs of functionals (`AffineLinearEmbedding.tensor_ext` and separation of points),
  decomposing each functional as `θ = (θ - θ 1 • 1) + θ 1 • 1`.

## Reduction to a finite primitive part

- `exists_mem_sq_eq_on W h1 hη hηV`: let `W` be finite-dimensional with `1 ∈ W`, and let
  `η ∈ augIdeal` vanish on every `x ∈ W` with `counit x = 0` and `x` killed by
  `augIdeal ^ 2`. Then some `θ ∈ augIdeal ^ 2` agrees with `η` on `W`. The proof uses the
  finite-dimensional duality `Subspace.dualCoannihilator_dualAnnihilator_eq` for the image
  of `augIdeal ^ 2` in `Module.Dual k W`.
- `convMul_apply_eq_zero_of_vanish`: if `a` is killed by `augIdeal ^ (m + 2)`, `η` is as in
  the previous lemma for `W = regularSpan {a, 1}`, and `Θ ∈ augIdeal ^ m`, then
  `(η * Θ) a = 0`. Indeed `(η * Θ) a = η (rightAct Θ a)` with `rightAct Θ a ∈ W`, so `η` may
  be replaced by `θ`, and `θ * Θ ∈ augIdeal ^ (m + 2)`.
- `prod_comp_eq_dualMonomial`, `sum_labelCount`: a product `∏ t, ξ (j t)` along a sequence
  `j : Fin M → Fin r` is the dual monomial of its label counts, of total degree `M`.
- `prod_apply_eq_zero` (**multilinear reduction**): suppose `η - ∑ η(bᵢ) • ξᵢ` vanishes on a
  set `V` for every `η ∈ augIdeal`. If `g` is killed by every dual monomial of degree `m + 1`
  and by every `η * Θ` with `η ∈ augIdeal` vanishing on `V` and `Θ ∈ augIdeal ^ m`, then `g`
  is killed by every product of `m + 1` elements of `augIdeal`. Each factor is split as
  `λ_t + η'_t` with `λ_t = ∑ ηₜ(bᵢ) ξᵢ`; the expansion term with only `λ`'s is a combination
  of dual monomials, and every other term has a factor `η'_t` vanishing on `V`.

## Main results

Assume `p` prime and `CharP k p`.

- `factorial_prod_ne_zero`: `∏ (δ i)!` is nonzero in `k` when all `δ i < p`.
- `mem_adjoin_primitive_of_mem_killedBy p hV m`: if every element of `augIdeal` has vanishing
  `p`-th power (`hV`), every `a` killed by `augIdeal ^ (m + 1)` lies in
  `Algebra.adjoin k {x | Bialgebra.IsPrimitiveElem k x}`.

  Proof as implemented, by induction on `m`. For `m = 0`, `a` is a scalar. In the step, let
  `W = regularSpan {a, 1}` and `V` the subspace of `x ∈ W` with `counit x = 0` killed by
  `augIdeal ^ 2`; its elements are primitive. Choose a basis `b` of `V` and functionals
  `ξ i ∈ augIdeal` with `ξ i (b j) = δᵢⱼ` (extend the coordinate functionals and subtract
  their value at `1`). With `M = m + 1`, define

  `f = ∑_{γ} (dualMonomial ξ γ a) * (∏ (γ i)!)⁻¹ • ∏_{v ∈ I γ} b v.1`,

  where `γ` ranges over exponent vectors with all entries `< p` and total `M`, and
  `I γ` is a finite index set with `γ i` copies of label `i`, so the last product is the
  monomial `b ^ γ`. By the Kronecker pairing (`PrimitiveProducts.md`) every dual monomial of
  degree `M` takes the same value on `a` and on `f`; for exponents with an entry `≥ p` the
  dual monomial is `0` because `ξ i ^ p = 0`. Elements `η * Θ` as above kill `a`
  (`convMul_apply_eq_zero_of_vanish`) and kill `f` (Leibniz expansion, since `η (b i) = 0`).
  The multilinear reduction and `mem_pow_closure` show that `a - f` is killed by
  `augIdeal ^ M`, so `a - f` lies in the generated subalgebra by induction, and `f` does by
  construction.
- `adjoin_primitive_eq_top p hV`: under `hV`, `A` is generated by its primitive elements.
  Every element is killed by some power of `augIdeal`
  (`exists_pow_augIdeal_apply_eq_zero`, `AugmentationIdeal.md`).
